solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Madrid is in her itinerary, but part can be cut off

indicators.note: only a portion of the run of words Madrid is in her itinerary is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone planning a Spanish trip warns that some legs of the journey may be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' points to letters lying across 'Madrid is in her itinerary'; 'but' and 'can be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit an heir is to cut them off from a legacy in a will.

clue.text: Expensive address

definitions.meaning: the word used to open a letter, as in a greeting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means costly and is also the standard salutation opening a letter.

clue.text: Often sitting in garden in street over a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part stands above the rest
the garden word sits inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: Someone who spends a lot of time seated in a garden on a street beside a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary person or job involves a great deal of sitting and little exercise.

clue.text: Mean to accompany a woman

indicators.note: one piece goes alongside the other, so they are joined side by side

parts.note: a norm is an average or mean

explanation.surface: Someone intends to escort a lady somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female given name, so any woman could be called it.

clue.text: It's the absolute end

parts.note: an exasperated exclamation that also describes the very farthest limit of something

explanation.definitionFit: The extreme is the outermost point or utmost degree, the absolute limit of anything.

clue.text: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy

definitions.text: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy

parts.words: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy
parts.note: a hypochondriac relishes being thought sick, so read the phrase as being famous for sickness

explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame means a bad reputation, and literally a reputation for illness.

clue.text: Mid-off on field in repulsive jumper

indicators.note: the central letter of the word off is taken

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at mid-off stands in a field wearing a hideous sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid-off' is a cricket fielding position, but here 'Mid' takes the middle letter of 'off'; 'jumper' is not a British sweater but a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a parasitic insect famed for its leaps and generally found disgusting.

clue.text: Exotic creature going around in a shopping centre

indicators.note: the whole phrase is turned so it reads backwards

parts.note: a mall is an indoor shopping centre

explanation.surface: An unusual animal is wandering loose in a shopping mall.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American camelid, an exotic animal to most readers.

clue.text: Standard position for a passing-out parade?

definitions.text: Standard position for a passing-out parade?

parts.words: Standard position for a passing-out parade?
parts.note: a standard is a flag, and passing out here means dying rather than graduating, so think of a flag lowered in mourning

explanation.definitionFit: Flags are flown partway down the pole as a sign of mourning for a death.

clue.text: As hot drinks they take some beating

definitions.text: As hot drinks they take some beating

parts.words: As hot drinks they take some beating
parts.note: take some beating means are hard to better, but these drinks are literally made with beaten eggs

explanation.definitionFit: Egg-flips are warm drinks of beaten egg with milk or spirits, a kind of nog.

clue.text: Summer danger

definitions.meaning: one who sums, someone doing addition
a venomous snake, a hazard in the countryside

explanation.definitionFit: An adder is both a person who totals figures and Britain's only venomous snake.

clue.text: Daily signal

definitions.meaning: to send a message or to give a sign of intent

explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a British paper, and to telegraph is to signal intentions in advance.

clue.text: Secret American manoeuvres

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A secret US military exercise is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in camera means conducted in private, out of public view, as in a closed court session.

clue.text: Easily shattered by loud jeer

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical mark for loud
to rail at is to scold or mock

explanation.surface: Someone fragile is crushed by a loud taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frail is delicate and liable to break easily.

clue.text: Mistake one cannot make twice

parts.note: a blunder so serious you do not survive it to repeat it

explanation.definitionFit: A deadly blunder ends everything, so there is no second chance to repeat it.

clue.text: A big hit, poetry that is in fashion

parts.note: to lam is to strike hard
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A smash hit poem is all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means fashionable or up to date.

clue.text: It measures resistance old headmaster confronted with hesitation

parts.note: HM is short for headmaster
met means faced or encountered
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An elderly head teacher faces opposition and hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an instrument for gauging electrical resistance, in units named after Ohm.

clue.text: The best government? Have a wry smile about it

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the little word it
twisted, so the letters of smile are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks about ideal rule and gives an ironic smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism favours rule by a select few, the supposed best, as a system of governing.

clue.text: Facial make-up used by the police

definitions.text: Facial make-up used by the police

parts.words: Facial make-up used by the police
parts.note: make-up here means composition, building up a face from parts, not cosmetics

explanation.definitionFit: An Identikit is a picture of a suspect assembled from stock facial features.

clue.text: Lamb, say, rambling is unfathomable

indicators.note: wandering about, so the letters stray into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lamb wandering aimlessly is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal literally describes a bottomless depth, something too deep to sound.

clue.text: 'Lear' in production set up with part of 'Hamlet'

indicators.note: the play's name is being staged, put together afresh in a new order
in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A staging of King Lear is mounted with a role from Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is a character, Ophelia's brother, in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Supporters set out for gripping ties

indicators.note: the supporters word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: fans are supporters of a team

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Football supporters set out wearing their club ties.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to tie or secure, a verb in the same third-person form.

clue.text: See fair play bloom

indicators.note: the letters are allowed to move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch honest sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant, so its flower is a bloom.

clue.text: Leave secretly for the match

parts.note: match means marriage, not a sports fixture

explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run off to marry without telling anyone do exactly this.

clue.text: Happen to come to mind

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to take place, and also an idea striking someone, as in it occurs to me.

clue.text: You never come to the end of this sort of ring

definitions.text: You never come to the end of this sort of ring

parts.words: You never come to the end of this sort of ring
parts.note: a jewellery band set all round with stones, and a span without end

explanation.definitionFit: An eternity ring has gems set all the way round and stands for endless love.

clue.text: Sounds like a strange letter in the post

indicators.note: the clue tells us to judge by the ear

parts.note: new means strange or unfamiliar, and the letter is L

explanation.surface: Something resembles an odd item of mail delivered by the postman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like mail but is the definition, the upright at the foot of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central upright or the end post supporting a stair handrail.

clue.text: In the guise of an afterthought, they're venomous

parts.note: as means in the role or guise of
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Things posing as a late addition turn out to be poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, Cleopatra's legendary choice.

clue.text: Unwinds — and makes it all over again

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both relaxes for pleasure and, read as re-creates, builds something afresh.

clue.text: Comes to parties

definitions.meaning: gatherings, especially after a funeral, or northern English holiday fairs

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means rouses from sleep, and the noun names vigils or festivities after a funeral.

clue.text: A good but uncommon description

parts.note: a word that in older use means excellent and also means seldom found

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unusual, and colloquially also splendid, as in a rare old time.

clue.text: Realise it's about Biblical Hebrews

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone comes to understand something about the ancient Jews.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites were the descendants of Jacob, the Hebrew people of the Old Testament.
